rules.statement: A feature turned on by a property or by the host's classpath never runs without what it needs (its module, its REQUIRED listener, its Redis connection): startup fails and names what to add. A module no feature uses needs nothing: a service behind a gateway (`cosec.pipeline.mode=gateway`) with JWT off, which wires no Redis data plane, starts without Redis although `cosec-cocache` is on its classpath.

rules.statement: On a Spring Cloud Gateway host in enforce mode, startup fails when an actuator endpoint other than health, of any kind (an operation endpoint, or a controller endpoint such as Spring Cloud Gateway's own gateway), is exposed over HTTP on the application port (management.server.port unset or the application's), naming the endpoints, what to set and the documentation, unless cosec.gateway.unprotected-endpoints lists it; that property never accepts gateway, wherever it is served. On a separate management port, or with the management server off, any endpoint may be exposed.

rules.source: RFC 0011 D2 (round 2 review of host and tools, M1)
rules.statement: The starter's startup checks run whatever spring.main.lazy-initialization says: every module check (STA-1), the actuator endpoint check (STA-2), the eviction policy check and monitor (SNP-3), the replica read check (RC1-47), the API key membership check (IDN-6), the pipeline mode check, the unknown property check and the control plane's own-authorization check fail startup under lazy initialization as they do without it, and the components that keep watching once the host runs (the eviction policy monitor, shadow reporting, control-plane maintenance, the listeners' metrics) start at startup. A check is a StartupCheck bean, which lazy initialization never defers; no auto-configuration of the starter declares a check any other way. A configuration none of them refuses starts under lazy initialization.
